clue.text: Large sum of money found in boring book?

definitions.meaning: slang for a very big figure, one with as many digits as a dialling code and line together
the dull directory listing subscribers and their lines, where every such figure is printed

explanation.surface: A dull tome turns out to hide a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a huge salary or price is 'telephone numbers' because it runs to many digits; the 'boring book' is the phone directory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the digits you dial and British slang for an enormous amount of cash.

clue.text: Live-in Head of State beheaded

indicators.note: taking the head off means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a president is the head of state in a republic

explanation.surface: A leader who lived in the palace has been executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live-in' is an adjective in the surface but the answer is read as someone who lives in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a person living in a place, so someone who lives in.

clue.text: "I'll get back to you", says English child with love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An English child promises to reply later, with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the dictionary abbreviation for child.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound returns to the speaker, so the quoted phrase is what it might say.

clue.text: Tear and kiss confused a star

indicators.note: jumbled up, so the letters of tear and kiss are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, the first word of the jumbled letters
taken as written, the second word of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A celebrity is left bewildered by a tearful kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a star' sounds like a celebrity, but it is the typographical mark, whose name means little star.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is named from Greek for little star and looks like one.

clue.text: Corset loosened for companion

indicators.note: a loosened garment has its parts rearranged, so the letters of corset are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone undoes a corset for a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a person who accompanies another, a synonym for a partner on an outing.

clue.text: Carefree heart is something achieved without difficulty

parts.note: easy can mean relaxed and untroubled
the meat of something is its core or essence

explanation.surface: A light heart makes tasks feel effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is an idiom for a target or task that can be overcome with no trouble.

clue.text: University about to elevate Blair before us

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: Tony Blair was the British Prime Minister, PM for short
taken as written, the pronoun supplies its own two letters

explanation.surface: A university is about to honour Tony Blair ahead of the rest of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, used by metonymy for the institution.

clue.text: Bad bankers fated to move into a guesthouse

indicators.note: the letters are made to move around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Failed bankers are doomed to relocate to cheap lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a small lodging offering a room and morning meal, a kind of guesthouse.

clue.text: Tasks involving the Queen in duties

indicators.note: the royal letters go in, placed within the word for duties

parts.note: excises are taxes or duties levied on goods
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Royal obligations involve various chores for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercises are set pieces of work for practice, so assignments or tasks.

clue.text: Egad! A contrary proverb!

indicators.note: going the opposite way, so the letters of egad a are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the mild oath supplies its own letters
taken as written, a single letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a saying that goes against expectation.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying expressing a general truth, a synonym for a saw.

clue.text: Model gives mince pie to me

indicators.note: mincing chops something up, so the letters of pie are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose letters are jumbled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a mince pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince pie' reads as the Christmas pastry, but mince is the instruction to jumble pie.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example or embodiment of a type, a synonym for a model.

clue.text: Oily map unfolded, showing where games were held

indicators.note: opening out a folded map shifts it about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A greasy map is opened to find an ancient sports venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in Greece was the sanctuary where the ancient Olympic contests took place.

clue.text: Hot fish for a scoundrel

parts.note: an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A spicy fish dish served to a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Heel is informal for a contemptible, untrustworthy man, a synonym for a cad.

clue.text: Bothered and is tense when getting dressed outside

indicators.note: dressed goes outside, wrapping round the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious and on edge while putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means upset or troubled, a synonym of worried or bothered.

clue.text: Ten returned to Labour organisation

indicators.note: sent back, so the word ten is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, the number word read backwards
labour as toil is work, not the political party

explanation.surface: Ten members came back to the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital L makes 'Labour' look like the British political party; here it just means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is a system of connected people or groups, a kind of organisation.

clue.text: Coming into contact with the system

parts.note: on means touching or in contact with a surface
taken as written
a way is a method or system of doing things

explanation.surface: Someone is getting in touch with the system.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the way is approaching or about to arrive, so coming.

clue.text: Jug for a baseball player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large jug for pouring liquids
second meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter

explanation.surface: A container suitable for a ballplayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a vessel with a handle and lip, and the thrower on a baseball diamond.

clue.text: A hundred absorbed by prelude in bar

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the hundred sits within prelude

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people take in an overture in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub or a musical bar beside prelude; it is the verb meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude is to prevent or rule out, a synonym for the verb bar.

clue.text: Sit with choir, which could be memorable

indicators.note: these letters could become another arrangement, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Sitting with the choir could be an unforgettable experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means important enough to be remembered by history, so notable or memorable.

clue.text: He doesn't run! He doesn't jump!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse entered in a flat race that never leaves the stalls
second meaning: a steeplechaser that fails to start, so never clears a fence

explanation.walkthrough: Both lines describe a horse withdrawn before the off, one in a flat race and one over fences; the word also means any idea with no chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is scratched or fails to start takes no part, neither running nor jumping.

clue.text: Fine point made by friendly Tory losing heart

parts.note: nice means pleasant and friendly

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the central letters of tory are removed

parts.note: taken as written, the party word whose middle goes

explanation.surface: A sharp argument is scored by an amiable Conservative who has lost his nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a subtle detail or distinction, a synonym for a fine point.

clue.text: Monkey King: he's superior to us

indicators.note: in a down entry the higher part comes first, so this letter group sits above the next

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey king boasts that he outranks us.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Rex, Latin for king.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a small brown Asian monkey widely used in research.

clue.text: Continent, as I am nearly

indicators.note: nearly all of the phrase as I am is used, its last letter dropped, so the answer sits within those words

parts.note: the phrase as written runs the letters straight through its words; all but the final letter are taken

explanation.surface: Someone says they are almost a whole continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent on Earth, an example of one.

clue.text: Teach me to break this knife

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A pupil asks to be taught how to snap a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Launching needs endless vitality and a swell

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: life means energy or liveliness
a swell is old slang for a fashionable gentleman, as is a toff

explanation.surface: A launch needs energy and a surge of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like a sea wave; it is old British slang for a well-dressed upper-class man, also called a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment a rocket leaves the ground, the start of a launch.

clue.text: Get rid of passion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dismiss someone from a job
second meaning: burning ardour or strong feeling

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like abandoning one's ardour; the two parts are separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sack an employee and intense emotional fervour.

clue.text: Former husband drawing back further

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: An ex-husband withdraws even more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing back' reads as one phrase meaning retreating; split it into drawing and back.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or more, a synonym of further as an adjective.

clue.text: Supports controlled by cutback

parts.note: under someone means subject to or controlled by them
split as cut and back: a snip is a cut, and back means it is read the other way

explanation.surface: Pillars are governed by spending reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' looks like one word for a reduction; split it into cut, giving snip, and back, the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpins means props up from below, as foundations do, a synonym of supports as a verb.
